comment: Declared allowances for API reference drift, enforced by tests/checks/reference-drift.test.js against the generated supabase/reference-coverage.json. Each number is a CEILING, not a target: a session that fixes rows lowers the ceiling in the same commit, and the ceiling can never rise without the owner agreeing to it in the commit message. This is the size-budget.json idiom applied to content: the gate cannot be turned on at zero because the work has not been done yet, but it can stop things getting worse from the day it lands.

LaunchPad Partner Portal API.note: Baseline 2026-08-13, tightened the same day, joined by the consumer dimension on 2026-08-14. phantom is now 0 and must stay there: the twelve wrong rows catalogued in docs/plan/20-API-REFERENCE.md were each traced to source and corrected, so a phantom row appearing again means the reference has drifted from the code rather than merely lagging it. gap reached 0 on 14 Aug and must stay there: every route the Angular portal calls is documented, measured by scripts/extract-calls.js rather than assumed, so this rising means the front end started calling something nobody wrote up. That is the one figure worth watching on every API change. absent 121 is the older, blunter number - it counts undocumented routes whether or not anything calls them, and now that gap is 0 every one of the 121 is a route with no front-end consumer: whole features nothing touches (Metrics, the unscoped OnboardingFlows mirror, ShoppingCart) plus four webhook receivers whose consumer is a third party. Lower absent as the register of those lands. undeclared_mirrors 0 as of 14 Aug and it must stay there: the v1 merchant collapse is now declared on the rows themselves, and a rule marked declared in gen-coverage.js earns nothing until the row it points at carries the badge - so this figure rising means someone added a collapse and did not say so. Deliberately NOT capped: uncalled (a fact about the API, not a defect) and stale_docs (which rises on purpose as the register lands) - a ceiling on either would make honest work fail the gate.

Unity Acquiring API.note: No source supplied, so the spec is not comparable and carries no phantom or absent figure. Nothing in it can be graded above 'stated' until a Unity source or live Swagger arrives; the single unverified badge understates that and should rise, deliberately, when the spec is graded honestly. duplicates 2: GET merchant-setup/merchants/{} and GET settlements/.../settlement-capabilities are each documented twice, once with {id} and once with {numId}. Whether Unity really accepts both forms or one row is a stray cannot be settled without a source, so neither was deleted - the question is in the spec's gap register. Drop to 0 when it is answered.

LaunchPad Inbound Onboarding API (planne.note: Design intent, not code, so it is not comparable by design. The eight gap badges are its open questions and shrink as the spin-out design settles.
